 Live Updates Updated Tue, Nov 3 2026 9:08 PM EST Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email Midterm elections 2026 live updates: Cooper flips N.C. Senate, Texas Senate seat 'leans' Dem
 Justin Papp Caleigh Keating Garrett Downs Kevin Breuninger Dan Mangan This is CNBC's live coverage of the 2026 midterm elections. 
 Polls are closing across the U.S. as voters are deciding control of Congress in an election that could define President Donald Trump 's final years in office.
 CNBC's Election Desk projects that control of the U.S. House "leans Democratic" and that Democrats will win a minimum of 205 of the chamber's 435 seats with Republicans winning at least 160. Democrats flipped the North Carolina Senate seat with a victory by former Gov. Roy Cooper.
 All 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats are at stake, as Republicans try to defend narrow majorities. Voter frustration with Trump's war in Iran , inflation , perceived government corruption and immigration policy could weigh down Republicans. But the GOP has the bulk of billionaire campaign spending.
 Deep-red Senate seats such as Kansas , South Carolina and Nebraska could be in play while Republicans could win in traditional Democratic strongholds such as Minnesota and New Hampshire. And toss-up races in states including Alaska, Iowa, Maine, Michigan, Ohio and Texas will determine who wins the gavels next Congress.
 The Associated Press provides vote data and race projections for CNBC. Polls began closing at 6 p.m. ET, with Alaska being the last to close at 1 a.m. ET. 
 What to know 
 Follow House results: Map 
 House control "leans Democratic" 
 Roy Cooper flips North Carolina Senate seat blue 
 Ossoff wins Georgia Senate race 
 Florida Senate "too close to call" 
 Here's when polls close next 
 South Carolina breaks state voting record 
 2 Min Ago South Carolina Senate race is 'too close to call'
 South Carolina's Senate race is "too close to call," according to CNBC's Election Desk.
 Republican Sen. Darline Graham , who was appointed to fill the rest of her brother Lindsey Graham's term after he died unexpectedly in July , is facing Democratic nominee Annie Andrews.
 The contest was not expected to be close, as South Carolina hasn't elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1998.
 But Graham struggled to consolidate support after a bitter GOP primary in August, and Andrews, a pediatrician, closed the gap. The Cook Report shifted the rating from "likely Republican" to "L ean R " on Oct. 20.
 — Justin Papp and Dan Mangan 
 8 Min Ago Texas Gov. Abbott has higher negatives than opponent, CNBC poll shows
 Texas Gov. Greg Abbott speaks to the media after casting his ballot in the midterm elections outside Travis County Community Center on October 19, 2026 in Del Valle, Texas. Sergio Flores | Getty Images In the hotly contested Texas governor's race, both candidates have the same 46% favorable rating, but incumbent Greg Abbott has higher negatives.
 The CNBC Voter Poll showed that 52% of respondents have an unfavorable view of the Republican Abbott, while just 2% have no opinion. Democratic challenger Gina Hinojosa has a 42% unfavorable rating, with 12% undecided.
 —Jeff Cox 
 8 Min Ago Dems estimated to win 205 House seats minimum, vs. 160 for GOP: CNBC Election Desk
 Democrats are now estimated to win a minimum of 205 seats in the U.S. House when all races are decided, CNBC's Election Desk projects.
 The update adds five seats to Democrats' column from the Election Desk's prior projection less than an hour earlier.
 Republicans remain estimated to win a minimum of 160 House seats, according to the desk.
 Control of the U.S. House still "Leans Democratic," per the Election Desk's projection.
 — Kevin Breuninger 
 9 Min Ago CNBC Election Desk: Texas Senate "leans" D
 State Rep. James Talarico, Texas Democratic U.S. Senate candidate, at left, and Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, the Republican U.S. Senate candidate. Getty Images The CNBC Election Desk projects that the Texas Senate race between Democratic state Rep. James Talarico and GOP Attorney General Ken Paxton is 'leaning D' as of 9 p.m. when the state's polls close. Talarico would be the first Democrat to win statewide in Texas since 1994. 
 — Justin Papp 
 14 Min Ago Sununu hurt by Trump ties in New Hampshire race
 John Sununu, Republican Senate candidate from New Hampshire, and his wife Kitty during a primary election night watch party in Manchester, New Hampshire, US, on Tuesday, Sept. 8, 2026. Mel Musto | Bloomberg | Getty Images John Sununu came up short in his quest for the New Hampshire Senate, hurt by his ties to Trump.
 The CNBC Voter Poll showed 56% of the state's voters found the Republican aligned too closely with Trump — a trend that repeated itself in multiple Senate races Tuesday. 
 Respondents gave victorious Democratic candidate Chris Pappas a 49%-47% favorability margin.
 —Jeff Cox 
 15 Min Ago Democrat Jamie Ager wins in North Carolina's 11th District, another pickup for Dems
 Democratic candidate for North Carolina's 11th congressional district Jamie Ager smiles, Monday, Aug. 11, 2025, in Fairview, N.C. Matt Kelley | AP Democrat Jamie Ager is projected to win election to North Carolina's 11th Congressional District on Tuesday according to the AP, defeating Republican state Rep. Jennifer Balkcom and flipping a Republican-held House seat.
 Ager, a western North Carolina farmer and businessman, won in a district that Trump carried by roughly 9.5 percentage points in 2024.
 The seat became an unexpected Democratic pickup opportunity after Republican Rep. Chuck Edwards dropped his reelection bid following a House Ethics Committee investigation that resulted in a recommendation that he be censured. Balkcom was selected to replace Edwards on the ballot.
 – Luke Fountain 
 21 Min Ago 17% of voters identify as democratic socialists, CNBC Voter Poll shows
 Democratic Socialists of America counter protesters hold signs and flags as they march, protesting an alt-right rally on August 5, 2018 in downtown Berkeley, California. Getty Images Nearly 1 out of 5 voters nationwide identifies as a democratic socialist, according to the CNBC Voter Poll.
 When asked if they considered themselves a democratic socialist, 17% responded yes. Of those respondents, 97% said they were supporting Democratic candidates.
 Voting was more mixed among the 82% that said they did not identify as democratic socialists. In this group, 53% said they backed Republicans, while 43% reported selecting Democrats.
 — Alex Harring 
 23 Min Ago Republican Sen. Ashley Moody projected to win Florida Senate special election
 Sen. Ashley Moody, R-Fla., takes her seat before the start of the Senate Judiciary Committee hearing on "Oversight of Jack Smith's Abuse of Authority and the Targeting of Republicans and Related Matters" in the Hart Senate Office Building on Tuesday, September 29, 2026. Bill Clark | Cq-roll Call, Inc. | Getty Images Incumbent Republican Sen. Ashley Moody is projected to win Florida's special Senate election, according to The Associated Press. 
 Moody is facing Democrat Angie Nixon.
 — Dan Mangan 
 25 Min Ago Michigan voters split on whether El-Sayed is too far left
 Voters fill out their ballots at a polling location inside Wayne Community College - Eastern Campus on the final day of early voting for the midterm election in Detroit, Michigan, US, on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. Emily Elconin | Bloomberg | Getty Images Michigan voters are split when it comes to whether far-left Democrat Abdul El-Sayed is too extreme, while considering his opponent too closely aligned with Trump.
 In the CNBC Voter Poll, 49% answered yes when asked whether El-Sayed's views were too extreme, while 51% said no. For his Republican opponent, 62% said Rogers is too supportive of the president. 
 The two are looking to replace retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters.
 — Jeff Cox 
 26 Min Ago Republican Mike Collins concedes Georgia Senate race to Democrat Jon Ossoff
 Representative Mike Collins, a Republican from Georgia and US Senate candidate, during an election night event in Atlanta, Georgia, US, on Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. Dustin Franz | Bloomberg | Getty Images Republican Mike Collins thanked his supporters and praised Trump as he conceded the Georgia Senate race to Democratic incumbent Sen. Jon Ossoff.
 "It's been an honor, an honor and a privilege to serve under the leadership of the best president in my lifetime," Collins told a crowd of supporters.
 "The results may not be what we wanted tonight, but y'all, that's OK," he said. "I'm going to continue to serve in whatever capacity I'm afforded, and I look forward to whatever the good Lord has in store for us."
 — Kevin Breuninger 
 32 Min Ago Susan Collins faces Trump stigma; opponent Jackson faulted for temper
 Senator Susan Collins, a Republican from Maine, speaks to members of the media while campaigning ahead of the midterm election at the Fryeburg Fair in Fryeburg, Maine, US, on Friday, Oct. 9, 2026. Graeme Sloan | Bloomberg | Getty Images Susan Collins' quest for a sixth term in the Senate could be complicated by perceived allegiance to Trump.
 The CNBC Voter Poll found that 58% of Maine respondents consider the Republican too much in line with the president. Collins is head of the powerful Appropriations Committee and is the only GOP senator from New England.
 Collins faces Democrat Troy Jackson, a former Maine Senate leader who stepped in to the race after scandals felled nominee Graham Platner in July. 
 Jackson has his own problems: 56% of respondents say he lacks the proper temperament to serve as senator. Jackson has been criticized for various outbursts and has a criminal record dating to when he was 19 involving a physical fight with another man. Jackson also told Collins to "shut up" during a debate.
 — Jeff Cox 
 36 Min Ago Florida Senate race leaning toward Republican incumbent Moody
 Florida's Senate race is leaning toward Republican Sen. Ashley Moody, according to CNBC's Election Desk.
 Moody is facing Democratic nominee Angie Nixon.
 — Dan Mangan 
 39 Min Ago Democrat Roy Cooper wins North Carolina Senate race, flips seat
 Roy Cooper, former governor of North Carolina and Democratic US Senate candidate for North Carolina, speaks during a "Make Things Cost Less" campaign kickoff event at Clouds Brewing on March 4, 2026 in Raleigh, North Carolina. Al Drago | Getty Images Former Democratic Gov. Roy Cooper won North Carolina's Senate race on Tuesday, the AP projects, defeating Republican Michael Whatley and flipping a Republican-held seat in a crucial victory for Democrats seeking control of the chamber.
 Cooper, who won the governorship in both 2016 and 2020 even as Trump carried North Carolina, defeated the former Republican National Committee chairman and close Trump ally in the race to replace retiring Republican Sen. Thom Tillis . 
 The victory marks the first time Democrats have won a North Carolina Senate election since 2008. Republicans had scaled back spending in the state as Cooper maintained a polling lead heading into Election Day.
 — Luke Fountain 
 43 Min Ago Florida GOP incumbents Luna and Salazar in tight races
 U.S. Rep. Anna Paulina Luna (R-FL), U.S. Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar (R-FL). Getty Images Two Florida House Republican incumbents, Reps. Anna Paulina Luna and Maria Elvira Salazar held leads of less than one percentage point soon after polls closed Tuesday and with more than 90% of vote reported in districts in which both GOP candidate was favored. 
 Democrats showed a strong early performance in Florida, as the AP projected them to win two seats — Florida's 14th and 22nd congressional districts — that were gerrymandered to favor Republicans. CNBC's Election Desk called Florida's Senate race too close to call.
 — Justin Papp 
 48 Min Ago Nebraska Senate race features two unpopular candidates
 Senator Pete Ricketts, a Republican from Nebraska (L), and Independent candidate for U.S. Senate Dan Osborn, of Nebraska. Getty Images The Nebraska Senate race features two candidates who aren't particularly well-liked by voters.
 Both Republican incumbent Pete Ricketts and his independent challenger, Dan Osborn, have net unfavorable views from the electorate, according to the CNBC Voter Poll. 
 In Ricketts' case, his favorable-to-unfavorable margin is 44%-54%, while for Osborn it's 45%-52%. For Ricketts, 55% of respondents said he was too close to Trump. In Osborn's case, the same percentage said he is too closely aligned with the Democrats. 
 — Jeff Cox 
 42 Min Ago Pappas wins New Hampshire Senate race, keeping crucial state blue
 Democratic US Senate candidate for New Hampshire Chris Pappas speaks during a campaign stop in Exeter, New Hampshire on October 17, 2026. Joseph Prezioso | Afp | Getty Images Rep. Chris Pappas has won an open Senate seat in New Hampshire, defeating former Republican Sen. John Sununu, AP projected.
 Pappas' victory keeps a critical state blue for Democrats following the retirement of Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, D-N.H. 
 A moderate, Pappas focused his campaign on tackling corruption and lowering costs.
 — Garrett Downs 
 53 Min Ago Democrat Kathy Castor wins reelection in Florida's 14th District
 Rep. Kathy Castor (D-FL) speaks during a news conference with Democratic members of the House Sustainable Energy and Environment Coalition on climate change on Capitol Hill on Nov. 13, 2025, in Washington, D.C. Andrew Harnik | Getty Images Democratic Rep. Kathy Castor won reelection in Florida's 14th Congressional District on Tuesday, the AP projects, defeating Republican Mike Beltran despite redistricting that transformed her Tampa-area seat into one Trump would have carried by roughly 10.5 percentage points in 2024.
 — Luke Fountain 
 58 Min Ago Democrat Jared Moskowitz wins reelection in Florida's 25th District
 Congressman Jared Moskowitz (D-FL) speaks at a press conference in Washington, DC on Sept. 8, 2025. Nathan Posner | Anadolu | Getty Images Democratic Rep. Jared Moskowitz won reelection in Florida's 25th Congressional District on Tuesday, the AP projects, defeating Republican Scott Singer despite redistricting that shifted the seat toward Republicans. Trump would have carried the district by about 9 percentage points in 2024. 
 — Luke Fountain 
 1 Hour Ago Trump policies to blame for inflation woes, CNBC poll finds
 U.S. President Donald Trump arrives to speak during a luncheon in the Rose Garden of the White House on Oct. 15, 2026, in Washington, D.C. Kevin Dietsch | Getty Images Trump is to blame for the nation's inflation problem, according to a strong majority of voters.
 Some 62% of respondents to the CNBC Voter Poll said that inflation, which has run above the Federal Reserve's 2% target for 5½ years, is due "more because" of Trump's policies. 
 That could be trouble for Republicans, as 79% said the cost of living is causing a severe or moderate hardship. Just 21% say inflation has caused them no hardship at all, the same amount that said it was causing a severe hardship.
 — Jeff Cox 
 1 Hour Ago House control 'leans Democrat,' CNBC Election Desk projects
 Control of the U.S. House is now leaning Democratic, CNBC's Election Desk projects.
 Democrats will win an estimated minimum of 200 seats when all races are decided, versus an estimated minimum of 160 seats for Republicans, according to the desk. 
 — Kevin Breuninger 
 1 Hour Ago New Hampshire Senate race 'leans Democratic,' CNBC Election Desk projects
 John Sununu, Republican Senate candidate from New Hampshire (L) and New Hampshire Democratic Senate candidate, U.S. Rep. Chris Pappas (D-NH). Getty Images CNBC's Election Desk projects the New Hampshire Senate election is leaning toward Democratic Rep. Chris Pappas . 
 In a battle of the moderates, Pappas is facing off against former New Hampshire Sen. John Sununu .
 Pappas has carved out a role as a moderate in Congress, and his campaign has focused on tackling corruption and lowering costs. Sununu, the brother of former Gov. Chris Sununu, has also run a moderate campaign touting bipartisanship despite having a Trump endorsement.
 — Garrett Downs 
 1 Hour Ago CNBC Election Desk: Florida Senate race 'too close to call' 
 Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Florida state Rep. Angie Nixon, at left, and Sen. Ashley Moody, R-Fla. Getty Images The CNBC Election Desk projects that the Florida Senate race between Republican Sen. Ashley Moody and Democratic candidate Angie Nixon is too close to call as of 8 p.m. Moody had been favored to win by FiftyPlusOne .
 — Justin Papp 
 1 Hour Ago Ossoff wins Georgia Senate race
 Georgia Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Sen. Jon Ossoff speaks to supporters and members of the media at a campaign event at the DeKalb History Center museum in Decatur, Georgia, Nov. 2, 2026. Megan Varner | Getty Images Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff won reelection in Georgia on Tuesday, the AP projects, defeating Republican Rep. Mike Collins and delivering a crucial victory for Democrats in their fight for control of the Senate.
 — Luke Fountain 
 1 Hour Ago Dearborn, Michigan, reports ballot shortages amid strong turnout, mayor says
 Voters wait in line to cast their ballots at a polling location inside Salina Intermediate School in Dearborn, Michigan, Nov. 3, 2026. Sarah Rice | Bloomberg | Getty Images Dearborn, Michigan, a major hub of Muslim voters, is reportedly running out of ballots amid strong turnout, according to the city's mayor.
 Mayor Abdullah Hammoud said on social media Tuesday that he heard reports that "some precincts have temporarily run out of ballots and that lines are longer than usual." He encouraged people in lines at polling locations to remain there while the city clerk restocks ballots.
 Hammoud said Dearborn's voter turnout had already surpassed the number seen in the 2022 midterm elections, in a separate post published Tuesday afternoon.
 In early voting alone, Hammoud said, residents cast about 22% more votes in the 2026 midterms than the 2024 general presidential election.
 Dearborn has one of the highest concentrations of Arab-Americans and Muslims in the U.S. High turnout there is expected to bode well for Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed — who, if victorious, would be the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress.
 — Alex Harring 
 2 Hours Ago Stock futures roll over, turn negative, as U.S. polls begin closing
 Earlier momentum in U.S. stock futures fizzled, with contracts tied to the major market benchmarks trading lower as Wall Street awaited results from the U.S. midterm elections. 
 As of 7:34 p.m. ET, Dow Jones Industrial Average futures were down 235 points, or 0.5%. S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 futures slipped 0.5% and 0.9%, respectively. 
 — Fred Imbert 
 2 Hours Ago Trump says U.S. has no immediate plan to strike Iran: Report
 President Donald Trump speaks to the media before he boards Air Force One at Joint Base Andrews, Maryland, Oct. 28, 2026. Kevin Dietsch | Getty Images The U.S. has no immediate plans to launch renewed strikes against Iran, Trump told The Financial Times in an interview Tuesday. 
 "We seem to be getting everything we want," Trump told the news outlet.
 Trump has floated the possibility of restarting hostilities with Iran after the midterm election .
 But the U.S. did launch air strikes against Iran on Monday, hitting targets on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, the flashpoint of the war that is now in its ninth month. A U.S. official described the action to MS NOW as a "defensive measure" in response to "Iranians using surface to air missiles against US assets."
 Trump told The Financial Times, "We're not really in a war" with Iran, claiming the U.S. has decimated Iran's capabilities. "But if you think about it, we haven't really had a war with them in a long time, six months, maybe more," he told the outlet.
 — Kevin Breuninger 
 2 Hours Ago CNBC Election Desk projects Georgia Senate race "likely D"
 Sen. Jon Ossoff, D-Ga., and the Republican Senate candidate, U.S. Rep. Mike Collins, R-Ga. Getty Images The CNBC Election Desk projects the Georgia Senate race between Democrat Sen. Jon Ossoff and GOP Rep. Mike Collins is "likely D" at 7:35 p.m. ET after polls in Georgia closed at 7. Georgia was initially viewed as a potential swing state for a Republican pickup, but Ossoff grew his lead as Election Day approached.
 — Justin Papp 
 2 Hours Ago 'Super en banc' rehearing sought in 9th Circuit in case over Trump admininistration threats to election workers
 The Service Employees International Union is seeking a so-called "super en banc" rehearing from all 29 judges on the the 9th Circuit U.S. Court of Appeals in a case where the labor union wants the Trump administration blocked from threatening election workers with criminal prosecution.
 Smaller panels of judges on the 9th Circuit have blocked a federal district court judge's order enjoining the administration from making such threats.
 The 9th Circuit has asked the Department of Justice to respond to SEIU's petition for the full-sized hearing.
 "Today, on Election Day, the en banc court gives federal officials the green light to threaten, intimidate and coerce state and local elections officials into setting aside ballots already cast," SEIU's petition says. "In doing so, it disregards the U.S. Constitution's allocation of authority over federal elections to the States, as limited by Congress only in circumstances inapplicable here."
 — Dan Mangan 
 2 Hours Ago Texas 2026: Races to watch
 watch now VIDEO 3:41 03:41 Texas 2026: The midterm races that could shape control of Congress News Videos Texas polls close at 9 p.m. ET, and the Senate race is one of the most anticipated this election. 
 Democratic State Rep. James Talarico is facing off against Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton for the seat long held by incumbent Republican Sen. John Cornyn . Cornyn lost the GOP primary after Trump endorsed Paxton.
 A Democrat has not won a statewide election in Texas since 1994, but this year, the party is hopeful it can change that. The race is one of several that could influence the balance of power and determine whether the Senate flips blue. 
 Elon Musk has given millions of dollars to Republican super PACS and donated $158 million to the Senate Leadership Fund to support Paxton. 
 In addition to the Senate race, Texas' 15th Congressional District is a "Toss Up," according to the Cook Report. This district will see the Democratic candidate, Tejano music star Bobby Pulido, challenge incumbent GOP Rep. Monica De La Cruz. Texas' 35th Congressional District is also expected to be a tight race, where Democrat Johnny Garcia and Republican Carlos De La Cruz fight for the district's open seat. Monica De La Cruz and Carlos De La Cruz are siblings. 
 — Irit Skulnik 
 2 Hours Ago Trump fumes about Fox News poll
 President Donald Trump speaks to reporters as he departs the White House, in Washington, Oct. 19, 2026. Finn Gomez | Getty Images Trump blasted Fox News for its polling.
 "The FoxNews Poll, always the worst, is so insulting with the questions they ask," Trump said in a Truth Social post.
 "Every question is a hit job, and every answer is "BULLS---" This has been going on for years."
 Trump earlier said he was taking a break from watching Fox News because he was annoyed by co-host Jessica Tarlov's voice.
 Trump soon after raged against the conservative network.
 "FoxNews Ratings are way down (27%!) because they're spending too much time covering the Trump Deranged Dumocrats! All of those people who used to watch Fox, and no longer do, get it. It's them, not me — My numbers are better than they have ever been," Trump wrote. "This happened once before, and Fox almost collapsed. It's happening again!"
 — Dan Mangan 
 2 Hours Ago Trump-focused voters largely show against the president
 Voters cast their ballots at a polling location in the Harlem neighborhood of New York, Nov. 3, 2026. Angelina Katsanis | Bloomberg | Getty Images Tuesday's midterms will decide which party controls each chamber of Congress, but the election is also a referendum of sorts on President Donald Trump as he nears the halfway point of his second term.
 In the CNBC Voter Poll, 59% of respondents said one reason for their vote in Tuesday's House races was to express support or opposition for the president. 
 The poll showed that 43% saw their ballots as a vote against Trump, while just 16% said their vote was to support the president. And 41% said the president was not a factor.
 — Jeff Cox 
 2 Hours Ago Michigan Senate showdown puts chamber control and Democrats' future at stake
 watch now VIDEO 3:16 03:16 Can Michigan tip the balance of Congress? News Videos Michigan's open Senate seat is a crucial Republican pickup opportunity and a must-win for Democrats hoping to retake the chamber. Progressive Democrat Abdul El-Sayed faces Republican former Rep. Mike Rogers in a state Trump narrowly carried in 2024.
 The race tests whether economic populism can win back working-class voters who have drifted toward Republicans. El-Sayed, who would become the nation's first Muslim senator, champions Medicare for All and taxing billionaires. Rogers has embraced Trump while strategically distancing himself in recent weeks amid political headwinds. 
 The race took a stunning turn Sunday when Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens, whom El-Sayed defeated in the primary, crossed party lines to endorse Rogers over disagreements about Israel. The defection could help Rogers court moderates, but it also energized El-Sayed's supporters, fueling a reported $2.4 million fundraising surge that day.
 The implications of the race also stretch to the 2028 presidential election . An El-Sayed victory would strengthen progressives' case that their economic message can win in Trump territory. A Rogers win would end a 32-year Republican Senate drought in Michigan and sharpen questions about whether Democrats' ideological divisions are costing them winnable races.
 — Luke Fountain 
 2 Hours Ago What's at stake for control of Congress
 watch now VIDEO 3:26 03:26 How 2026 midterms will affect Congress News Videos Which party takes control of the House and the Senate will not only determine what bills get passed in the next Congress, but also how Trump opts to govern.
 CNBC's Garrett Downs broke down what different scenarios of congressional control mean for the next two years and highlighted key swing districts that could help determine which party wins control of the House.
 If Republicans win the House and Senate, Trump will continue to enact his legislative agenda with little resistance from Congress. If Democrats win one or both chambers, gridlock is expected, with necessary funding measures potentially being the only bills to pass. If they win control, Democrats could conduct wide-ranging investigations into Trump and corporate executives, and the president could issue more executive orders.
 — Caleigh Keating 
 2 Hours Ago Moody's: War with Iran costs average U.S. household more than $2,000
 Dado Ruvic | Reuters The U.S. war with Iran had cost the average American household $2,147 as of late October, according to an analysis from Mark Zandi, chief economist at Moody's Analytics.
 Here's Zandi's breakdown of that total:
 Additional energy costs: $1,227
 Higher borrowing costs: $559
 Increased military costs: $361
 Among respondents in Tuesday's CNBC Voter Poll, 74% said Iran was a crucial or major factor in their vote for Congress, and 62% said the U.S. made the wrong decision in taking military action against the country, according to the latest results.
 — Alex Harring 
 2 Hours Ago Senate Republicans launch 'recount fund' in Alaska as DOJ probe intensifies
 U.S. Sen. Dan Sullivan, R-Alaska, and former U.S. Rep. Mary Peltola, the Democratic U.S. Senate candidate. Justin Sullivan | Getty Images Senate Republicans launched the National Republican Senatorial Committee "recount fund" on Tuesday as Sen. Dan Sullivan faces Democrat Mary Peltola — and another candidate named Dan Sullivan — in Alaska's closely watched Senate race, according to a new Federal Election Commission filing .
 "We will be ready for all contingencies, including recounts, should they be necessary," NRSC Communications Director Joanna Rodriguez told CNBC.
 The fund could expand to other races if recounts are needed, according to a person familiar with the matter. The move comes as the Justice Department investigates allegations that Democrats recruited the second Dan Sullivan to siphon votes from the Republican incumbent. 
 Prosecutors sent target letters to more than a dozen people, including leaders of Democratic law firm Elias Law Group, on Tuesday. A federal judge separately rejected the DOJ's bid to delay certification of Alaska's results on Sunday.
 — Luke Fountain 
 2 Hours Ago Follow the House results as they roll in with CNBC's nationwide election map 
 — Kevin Breuninger 
 2 Hours Ago S&P 500 futures tick higher as traders await U.S. midterm election results
 Stock futures were mostly higher , lifted by a rally in chipmaker AMD, as traders awaited results from the U.S. midterm elections.
 S&P 500 futures gained 0.1%, along with Nasdaq-100 futures . Dow Jones Industrial Average futures lagged, losing 36 points, or 0.1%. 
 — Fred Imbert 
 2 Hours Ago Trump's tariffs get low marks from voters
 Trucks enter a shipping berth at the Port of Los Angeles, in Los Angeles, Oct. 14, 2026. Justin Sullivan | Getty Images Voters took a dim view of President Donald Trump's tariffs heading into the midterms.
 Respondents to the CNBC Voter Poll said the duties are damaging both the national and local economies: 65% said tariffs have hurt the national economy, while only 22% say they helped. 
 Asked about the impact on the economy in their area, voters' responses were similar, with 63% saying they hurt and only 15% indicating they helped.
 —Jeff Cox 
 The CNBC Voter Poll is a collaborative effort across several news organizations to produce the next generation of exit poll data. Drawing on about 100,000 interviews being conducted by phone, online, and in-person at polling locations, it provides a detailed snapshot of how people voted and what key issues may have shaped their decisions .
 2 Hours Ago Buttigieg: Economic pain tied to Trump administration corruption
 watch now VIDEO 3:37 03:37 People are fired up for change, says Pete Buttigieg on midterms Squawk Box Ahead of election results Tuesday, Biden administration Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg said Americans are "fired up for change" and align more with Democratic policies this election cycle, with Republicans telling him of their plans to vote for Democratic candidates.
"I think the general view of the American people [is] much more aligned with the Democratic candidates," Buttigieg told CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" on Tuesday. "You look at the polls, you look at the prediction markets. I look at the energy on the ground and the faces of the people I'm speaking to at these events, and people are pretty fired up for change."
 Buttigieg defended some plans for investigations of the Trump administration and corporate executives if Democrats take control of Congress, saying Congress' duty to expose corruption and defend the rule of law rendered them necessary.
 "That sort of corruption and that sort of just, frankly, twisted nature of today's Washington, really undermines any ability to have healthy markets and any ability to have confidence in our political system," Buttigieg said. 
"I think a lot of the economic pain that Americans are feeling is connected to some of the corruption that has infiltrated our political system, and I do think Congress has a duty to expose that corruption and make sure it can't happen again."
 — Caleigh Keating 
 2 Hours Ago Economy dominates voter concerns
 A sign displays the prices of gasoline and diesel fuel at a Quiktrip gas station in Atlanta, Nov. 2, 2026. Elijah Nouvelage | Bloomberg | Getty Images Americans are concerned about an economy they feel is tilted toward the rich, and they trust Democrats more to fix it, according to the CNBC Voter Poll for Tuesday's midterm elections.
 The survey showed a dim view of current conditions, with 75% calling the economy not so good or poor while 25% rated it excellent or good. Along with that, 69% said benefits flow to the wealthy, while just 18% described their family financial situation as better than it was two years ago.
 Worries over gas prices dominated: 87% said they were either somewhat or very concerned over costs at the pump.
 When it comes to party, 43% of respondents said they trust Democrats more on the economy, while 38% backed Republicans and 20% said neither.
 —Jeff Cox 
 The CNBC Voter Poll is a collaborative effort across several news organizations to produce the next generation of exit poll data. Drawing on about 100,000 interviews being conducted by phone, online, and in-person at polling locations, it provides a detailed snapshot of how people voted and what key issues may have shaped their decisions. 
 3 Hours Ago How Trump is watching the midterms
 The White House is seen on the midterm election day on November 3, 2026 in Washington, DC. Kevin Carter | Getty Images News | Getty Images Trump will be watching the election results roll in from the White House, according to his official schedule.
 The president earlier in the day met with the U.S. ambassador to Portugal and participated in multiple policy meetings, none of which were opened to the press, the schedule shows.

 5 Hours Ago Why stocks usually rise after midterms
 Douglas Rissing | Istock | Getty Images Markets may be nervous ahead of the midterm elections, but history suggests that anxiety often fades quickly. Recent CNBC analysis found that the S&P 500 gained an average of 13.7% in the year following midterm elections, with positive returns in 91% of cases.
 "Once you are through it, it's a big relief, and markets tend to do pretty well," Ryan Detrick of Carson Group told CNBC.
 A Nov. 3 Deutsche Bank note points to a similar pattern. The bank said midterm years are usually the weakest part of the four-year cycle because of political uncertainty, which eases once the election is over. "The market is buying a 'known' outcome," the bank said. The usual result is divided government and gridlock, which reduces the risk of major policy changes.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon S&P 500 stock performance Deutsche Bank looked at the S&P 500's performance over the 12 months following every midterm vote since 1930 and found that the index rose after 22 of 24 midterms. The analysis showed that historically the broad market and most individual stocks are likely to be higher in 12 months, with both median and average gains in double digits.
 "But given today's concentration, whether the run extends to a 22nd consecutive positive post-midterm period likely depends on the performance of just a handful of stocks," the bank said.
